# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1350
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1350
- **Title**: ci(1267): path-triggered macOS exclusion-zone leg — JS-engine tests run pre-merge (N1, first slice)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1267-nightly-premerge-catch` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +80
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T21:34:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T00:03:51Z

## PR Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge, declaratively:

- **`changes` job**: new `exzone` output (same inline-grep pattern as `perf`/`usagefold`) — fires when a PR diff touches `flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded `flutter_app/test/apps/**` family, `flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart`, or `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` (the external `js_widget_runtime` pin — see path-mapping note).
- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A PR touching only `lib/src/` core pays nothing.
- Docs: ci.yml header leg inventory + AGENTS.md §Quality gates.

**Path-mapping note (body vs repo @ 6d1a300):** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime). Its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin, which the trigger covers; a lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: it is the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307, fix commit be413ff5d); it is pure CI-config-as-code (path filters only — no scheduling, no dispatch; SM/owner pushes still own every run, §4b respected); and it needs no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) nor new bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18; five red nights, zero trackers.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive 2026-10-05): merge queue or merge-bot-synthesized trees; subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Static**: ruby-YAML structural check (45 jobs; all 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; `exzone` output declared; report line + fail-loop kv wired; job steps/SDK pins identical to the nightly leg's).
- **Classifier behavior**: the exact grep replayed against synthetic positives (all 5 trigger path families fire; `flutter_app/lib/apps.dart`, `pubspec.lock`, `lib/src/**`, `packages/fa_ui/**` correctly do NOT) **and against the real motivating diffs**: #1273 (989dfbfff — the regression that became gh-1307) and the gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) **both trigger** the leg.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. macOS runner behavior risk is low (step-for-step mirrors the nightly leg that already passes weekly). No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge, declaratively:

- **`changes` job**: new `exzone` output (same inline-grep pattern as `perf`/`usagefold`) — fires when a PR diff touches `flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded `flutter_app/test/apps/**` family, `flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart`, or `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` (the external `js_widget_runtime` pin — see path-mapping note).
- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A PR touching only `lib/src/` core pays nothing.
- Docs: ci.yml header leg inventory + AGENTS.md §Quality gates.

**Path-mapping note (body vs repo @ 6d1a300):** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime). Its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin, which the trigger covers; a lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: it is the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307, fix commit be413ff5d); it is pure CI-config-as-code (path filters only — no scheduling, no dispatch; SM/owner pushes still own every run, §4b respected); and it needs no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) nor new bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18; five red nights, zero trackers.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive 2026-10-05): merge queue or merge-bot-synthesized trees; subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment.

- **Classifier behavior**: the exact grep replayed against synthetic positives (all 5 trigger path families fire; `flutter_app/lib/apps.dart`, `pubspec.lock`, `lib/src/**`, `packages/fa_ui/**` correctly do NOT) **and against the real motivating diffs**: #1273 (989dfbfff — the regression that became gh-1307) and the gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) **both trigger** the leg.

# pr-1350: ci(1267): path-triggered macOS exclusion-zone leg — JS-engine tests run pre-merge (N1, first slice)

## Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge, declaratively:

- **`changes` job**: new `exzone` output (same inline-grep pattern as `perf`/`usagefold`) — fires when a PR diff touches `flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded `flutter_app/test/apps/**` family, `flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart`, or `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` (the external `js_widget_runtime` pin — see path-mapping note).
- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A PR touching only `lib/src/` core pays nothing.
- Docs: ci.yml header leg inventory + AGENTS.md §Quality gates.

**Path-mapping note (body vs repo @ 6d1a300):** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime). Its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin, which the trigger covers; a lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: it is the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307, fix commit be413ff5d); it is pure CI-config-as-code (path filters only — no scheduling, no dispatch; SM/owner pushes still own every run, §4b respected); and it needs no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) nor new bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18; five red nights, zero trackers.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive 2026-10-05): merge queue or merge-bot-synthesized trees; subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Static**: ruby-YAML structural check (45 jobs; all 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; `exzone` output declared; report line + fail-loop kv wired; job steps/SDK pins identical to the nightly leg's).
- **Classifier behavior**: the exact grep replayed against synthetic positives (all 5 trigger path families fire; `flutter_app/lib/apps.dart`, `pubspec.lock`, `lib/src/**`, `packages/fa_ui/**` correctly do NOT) **and against the real motivating diffs**: #1273 (989dfbfff — the regression that became gh-1307) and the gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) **both trigger** the leg.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. macOS runner behavior risk is low (step-for-step mirrors the nightly leg that already passes weekly). No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; only when the diff touches the exclusion zone —
#               the surface the ubuntu leg skips, otherwise nightly-only)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # PR-only (issue #1267 N1): a diff touching the macOS exclusion zone
      # runs the JS-engine test family pre-merge on macos (the surface the
      # ubuntu leg skips and otherwise only nightly exercises).
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui trajectory widgets, CLI
          # trajectory parts, the fah entrypoint, its tests, and the app's
          # session load path.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/cli/trajectory_|^bin/fah\.dart$|^test/(integration/)?trajectory/|^flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service(_sessions)?\.dart$)'; then
            echo "perf=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # gh-1241 REG-1: the usage fold consumes the trajectory ledger's
          # model_request_summary records and the session chain's shape —
          # a red usage-fold suite blocks the merge even when the regular
          # legs are green.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/session/|^lib/src/usage/|^test/usage/|^lib/src/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger\.dart$)'; then
            echo "usagefold=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion zone. The ubuntu flutter-tests
          # leg runs this family but every engine-dependent test SKIPS there
          # (native_test_guard.dart finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner);
          # the tests truly execute only in the nightly macOS leg — the hole
          # #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an apps/engine regression merged
          # green, went red the same night). The issue's packages/
          # js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its bumps arrive
          # via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
  # only prove the SBPL PROFILE TEXT (unit + guard/profile parity) — the
  # kernel's last-match-wins read/write enforcement of rw mounts under a
  # read-denied prefix needs a real `sandbox-exec` run, which exists only on
  # macOS. Both live suites skip with a NAMED reason wherever they cannot
  # run (no sandbox-exec / already-sandboxed host / HOME outside /Users) —
  # the skip lands in the job log, never silent; this leg is where they
  # actually execute. The leg is a real gate input: `quality-gate` NEEDS it
  # and fails the merge when it fails (a skip — a diff with no core paths —
  # passes, like every other optional leg).
  #
  # Skip condition note (PR #718 review): gating on `core` covers
  # `shared`-only diffs too — the classifier maps a shared/unknown path to
  # ALL nine stages, `test-core` among them, so `core=true` falls out and
  # this leg runs; only docs-only diffs (or non-PR context mismatches)
  # skip it.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cube-kernel-live:
    name: Cube kernel live (macOS)
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Content-addressed native-assets hook downloads (sqlite3 et al) are
      # hash-verified on reuse — cache them so a GitHub release-asset
      # brownout (504 bodies hashed as mismatches, 2026-09-21) can't
      # re-break every job that re-downloads.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1350
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1350
- **Title**: ci(1267): path-triggered macOS exclusion-zone leg — JS-engine tests run pre-merge (N1, first slice)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1267-nightly-premerge-catch` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +80
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T21:34:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T00:03:51Z

## PR Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge, declaratively:

- **`changes` job**: new `exzone` output (same inline-grep pattern as `perf`/`usagefold`) — fires when a PR diff touches `flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded `flutter_app/test/apps/**` family, `flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart`, or `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` (the external `js_widget_runtime` pin — see path-mapping note).
- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A PR touching only `lib/src/` core pays nothing.
- Docs: ci.yml header leg inventory + AGENTS.md §Quality gates.

**Path-mapping note (body vs repo @ 6d1a300):** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime). Its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin, which the trigger covers; a lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: it is the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307, fix commit be413ff5d); it is pure CI-config-as-code (path filters only — no scheduling, no dispatch; SM/owner pushes still own every run, §4b respected); and it needs no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) nor new bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18; five red nights, zero trackers.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive 2026-10-05): merge queue or merge-bot-synthesized trees; subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Static**: ruby-YAML structural check (45 jobs; all 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; `exzone` output declared; report line + fail-loop kv wired; job steps/SDK pins identical to the nightly leg's).
- **Classifier behavior**: the exact grep replayed against synthetic positives (all 5 trigger path families fire; `flutter_app/lib/apps.dart`, `pubspec.lock`, `lib/src/**`, `packages/fa_ui/**` correctly do NOT) **and against the real motivating diffs**: #1273 (989dfbfff — the regression that became gh-1307) and the gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) **both trigger** the leg.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. macOS runner behavior risk is low (step-for-step mirrors the nightly leg that already passes weekly). No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; only when the diff touches the exclusion zone —
#               the surface the ubuntu leg skips, otherwise nightly-only)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:

    outputs:

      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}

Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1350
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1350
- **Title**: ci(1267): path-triggered macOS exclusion-zone leg — JS-engine tests run pre-merge (N1, first slice)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1267-nightly-premerge-catch` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +80
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T21:34:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T00:03:51Z

## PR Description

Part of #1267

## Slice delivered: N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg (AC1)

By #177 design the ubuntu PR leg never *exercises* the JS-engine suites: `flutter_app/test/apps/**` run there, but every engine-dependent test **skips** (`native_test_guard.dart` finds no QuickJS `.so` on a bare runner). That surface executed **only** in the nightly macOS leg — the hole **#1309** escaped through (gh-1307: #1273's engine fix merged green and went red the same night; gh-1266 is the same class). This PR closes that hole pre-merge, declaratively:

- **`changes` job**: new `exzone` output (same inline-grep pattern as `perf`/`usagefold`) — fires when a PR diff touches `flutter_app/lib/apps/**`, `lib/src/js_ext/**`, the guarded `flutter_app/test/apps/**` family, `flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart`, or `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` (the external `js_widget_runtime` pin — see path-mapping note).
- **New `flutter-app-exzone` leg**: `macos-latest`, runs `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` where JavaScriptCore actually loads — the guard resolves true, so the engine-dependent tests *run* instead of skip. Same SDK/placeholder incantation as nightly's `flutter-app-macos` leg; 25 min cap.
- **Quality gate**: folded into the aggregate `needs` + report + fail-loop (skip-tolerant like every path-gated leg) → AC1's *required-and-green* via the repo's one-required-check design. A PR touching only `lib/src/` core pays nothing.
- Docs: ci.yml header leg inventory + AGENTS.md §Quality gates.

**Path-mapping note (body vs repo @ 6d1a300):** the issue's `packages/js_widget_runtime/**` no longer exists in-repo — `js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.154` is an **external git dep** (IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime). Its in-repo arrival surface is the `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin, which the trigger covers; a lockfile-only resolve is deliberately N2 territory, not this slice.

## Why this slice first

The body lists no explicit priority among N1–N4. N1 is the highest-value/lowest-risk: it is the only rule whose motivating incident **recurred after the issue was filed** (#1309/gh-1307, fix commit be413ff5d); it is pure CI-config-as-code (path filters only — no scheduling, no dispatch; SM/owner pushes still own every run, §4b respected); and it needs no repo-state change (N2 commits a lockfile) nor new bot/queue machinery (N3 filer, N4 merge snapshots).

## Remaining goal map (NOT in this PR)

- **N2** — commit `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `--enforce-lockfile` in every build leg, path-triggered linux+windows release-build smoke on lockfile changes (AC2).
- **N3** — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation (AC3): the filer is silently dead since #466 closed 2026-09-18; five red nights, zero trackers.
- **N4** — merge-snapshot gating + nightly test-leg elimination (AC5, owner directive 2026-10-05): merge queue or merge-bot-synthesized trees; subsumes the #1282 dispatch-time binaries wiring per the issue comment.
- Closing #1267 also requires #1265 + #1266 closed (AC4).

## Verification (disclosure)

- **Static**: ruby-YAML structural check (45 jobs; all 28 `quality-gate` needs resolve; `exzone` output declared; report line + fail-loop kv wired; job steps/SDK pins identical to the nightly leg's).
- **Classifier behavior**: the exact grep replayed against synthetic positives (all 5 trigger path families fire; `flutter_app/lib/apps.dart`, `pubspec.lock`, `lib/src/**`, `packages/fa_ui/**` correctly do NOT) **and against the real motivating diffs**: #1273 (989dfbfff — the regression that became gh-1307) and the gh-1266 fix (38303cfbb) **both trigger** the leg.
- **Not verified here**: actual macOS leg execution — CI-dispatch ban (§4b); the leg runs when SM schedules this PR's validation. macOS runner behavior risk is low (step-for-step mirrors the nightly leg that already passes weekly). No dart/flutter executed on this host (EPERM/137 guard).
